information_for_contributors: Produced by `typr syntax --target tmlanguage` from the syntax manifest in
crates/typr-core/src/components/syntax/mod.rs, the single source of truth for
TypR's lexemes. Edit the manifest and re-run `typr syntax --write`; CI runs
`typr syntax --check` and fails on a hand-edited grammar.
name: typR

annotations.comment: Visibility/interop annotations (RFC-TR-032). Ahead of the `@T` interface sigil and of any bare-`@` rule, both of which would eat their `@`.

comments.comment: TypR comments are `#` only — never `//`, which the parser rejects outright (`wrong_comment` in parsing/mod.rs). The lookahead is the one place a regex grammar has to guess where the parser uses context: `#N` and `#Self` are the Number kind sigil, so they are left to `types.sigil-generic`; anything else after `#` opens a comment.

constants.comment: Both spellings are real: `parsing/elements.rs` accepts the R form and the lowercase TypR form. No `NaN`/`Inf` — the parser has a tag for neither.

functions.call.comment: After every keyword rule, so `if (`/`while (` stay keywords.

keywords.block.comment: Escape-hatch and test block heads: `R { ... }`, `JS { ... }`, `Test { ... }`, `Test[...]`. Delimiter-guarded for the same reason as `types.constructor` — and `R` in particular is a single uppercase letter, i.e. also a valid generic name, so an unguarded rule would fight `types.generic`.

keywords.cast.comment: `as!` first, or the `as` alternative eats its prefix.

keywords.control.comment: No `continue`: the loop-skip keyword is `next;` (R spelling), `parsing/elements.rs::next_exp`.

keywords.declaration.comment: No `impl`/`trait`/`struct`/`enum`/`where`/`mut`/`pub`: none has ever existed in TypR — they were Rust leftovers in the hand-written grammars. Visibility is spelled with the `@pub`/`@export` annotations.

numbers.float.comment: `parsing/elements.rs::number` — digits, a dot, digits. No exponent form exists.

operators.arithmetic.comment: No `^`/`++`/`--`/`**`/`//`: `op()` recognizes none of them. `^` is the String kind sigil and nothing else — the hand-written grammars listed it as exponentiation, which TypR does not have.

operators.arrow.comment: Ahead of comparison and arithmetic, which own `-`, `=` and `>`.

operators.assign.comment: Bare `=` is never an infix operator in TypR — only a binder, a named-field separator and a default-value separator. Last of the `=`-shaped rules so `==`, `=>` and `!=` are already claimed.

operators.bind.comment: Ahead of comparison, whose `<` would otherwise split `<-`.

operators.custom.comment: R-style custom infix (`operators.rs::custom_op`). Ahead of the bare `%` modulo.

operators.logical.comment: After comparison, so `!=` is not read as `!` then `=`. `|` belongs to `operators.type-union`, which it doubles as.

operators.pipe.comment: No `|>>`: it has no type-checking or transpiling arm and no stdlib signature — see the tokenizer purge note on `operators.rs::op`.

operators.spread.comment: `...` runtime spread / variadic, `..` nominal spread (`Point:{ ..source }`). Longest-first inside the rule, and ahead of `operators.access`'s `.`.

strings.raw-r.comment: `extern (...) -> T r#"..."#` raw R body — verbatim, no escape processing. Ahead of `comments` so its inner `#` never opens one.

types.builtin.comment: No `Option`/`Result`/`List`/`Matrix`: TypR has none of them. These are the names usable bare in a type position; the ones that only exist in front of a delimiter are in `types.constructor` and `keywords.block`.

types.builtin-indexed.comment: `df` is a type name the parser accepts bare too (`parsing/types.rs::dataframe_type`), but `df` is also the single most common data-frame *variable* name in R. Coloring it only in `df[...]` under-colors a bare `x: df` annotation; the alternative over-colors every `df` in every program, which is worse. `dataframe`, the unambiguous spelling, stays in `types.builtin`.

types.constructor.comment: The parser only ever matches these glued to their opening delimiter (`c(`, `seq[`, `Class(`, `library(`), so the delimiter is part of the rule. Without it, every variable named `c` would be colored as a builtin.

types.sigil-generic.comment: Sigil + generic. A generic name is a *single* uppercase letter or `Self` (`parsing/types.rs::upper_case_generic`), so the rule stops there instead of running on into a PascalCase alias.

variables.other.comment: An identifier starts lowercase-or-underscore and continues in `[A-Za-z0-9_]` — no dots, unlike R (`parsing/elements.rs::starting_char`/`body_char`). `data.frame` is a single dedicated tag, not an identifier.

variables.parameter.comment: `(?!:)` keeps the `x` of `x::y` out — that is namespace access, not an annotation.
